transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-09 15:00 PST
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Lena Park (Mariposa CTO), Raj Patel (Mariposa ML Eng), Maya Ruiz (Mariposa DevOps)
---
Summary: Quick discovery focused on using Redwood's PLG quickstart hosted API to get a POC running quickly. Emphasis on time-to-first-token, free credits, security controls (SSO/KMS), and expected latency for chat API under 200ms p95.

00:00 Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we've got about 40 minutes, excited to see how quickly we can get a POC in our support flow.
00:12 Sophie Chen: Great, Lena. Quick intros — I'm Sophie, AE for Redwood, and Diego is our solutions engineer. We'll keep this focused on PLG quickstart and options to scale to Dedicated or Private later.
00:25 Diego Morales: Hi all, happy to dig into the technical bits and bench methodology.
00:30 Raj Patel: Raj here, I run our ML infra. We use managed endpoints today and care a lot about latency and cost.
00:36 Maya Ruiz: Maya, DevOps — we handle VPCs and security requirements.
00:42 Sophie Chen: Agenda: 1) understand your success criteria, 2) quickstart/free credits and time-to-first-token, 3) discuss Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, security, and 4) next steps. Does that work?
00:52 Lena Park: Yes. Our goal is a chat assistant in our support UI that answers short queries, high concurrency during peak — maybe a few hundred concurrent small requests. Time to value is critical; engineers should see first token same day.
01:12 Sophie Chen: That's exactly what PLG quickstart is designed for — self-serve signup, free credits to prototype, and a Node sample app that usually yields first token in under an hour for an engineer.
01:28 Raj Patel: For the sandbox, what's the provisioning flow? Any legal or security checks blocking access?
01:34 Sophie Chen: For the quickstart we provision a sandbox API key after signup — minimal friction. For enterprise orgs we can enable SSO and scoped keys. We'll still provide a hosted sandbox for prototyping.
01:50 Maya Ruiz: Network-wise, quickstart will be external HTTPS calls, right? No VPC peering for the sandbox?
01:55 Diego Morales: Correct, the prototyping flow uses hosted HTTPS endpoints. VPC peering and private networking are available for Dedicated/Private production setups.
02:07 Raj Patel: Latency expectations — for our short responses (<=256 tokens) we need p95 under 200ms. Can Hosted hit that?
02:15 Diego Morales: On optimized kernels and quantized 7B/13B variants we often see sub-150ms p95 for short sequences in our benchmarks, but that's workload-dependent. We'll run a bench with your prompts to give empirical numbers.
02:35 Lena Park: Cost tradeoffs — we prefer open models. Are there recommendations to balance latency cost?
02:41 Sophie Chen: Yes — Redwood Optimize suggests batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization profiles. For many workloads a 7B quantized model gives good latency/cost balance. We'll include cost estimates for Hosted vs Dedicated.
03:00 Raj Patel: Do you provide SDKs? We're Node + Go heavy.
03:04 Sophie Chen: We have official Node and Python SDKs; Go via REST is straightforward. Quickstart includes a Node sample app.
03:14 Maya Ruiz: Compliance: SOC2, ISO, audit logs — do you offer these?
03:18 Sophie Chen: We have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001. Hosted customers can get audit logs; for Private you can route logs to your S3 and integrate with your SIEM. We'll share the security pack after the call.
03:36 Raj Patel: If we start on Hosted for the pilot, how fast can we then move to Dedicated?
03:40 Diego Morales: Typically Dedicated can be provisioned in a few weeks, depending on commit and capacity. Private (VPC/on-prem) takes longer due to networking and procurement.
03:50 Lena Park: For the pilot, we'd like Redwood to guarantee some performance targets for the bench window. Is that doable?
03:56 Sophie Chen: For short pilots we can set clear monitoring and a performance commitment for the bench run; Diego will share the checklist and harness so results are repeatable.
04:10 Diego Morales: I'll provide a benchmark harness, concurrency scripts, and sample prompts. We recommend running from your infra to get realistic network variance.
04:25 Raj Patel: Can you explain the caching behavior — KV cache/prefix caching — and how it affects cost?
04:30 Diego Morales: Sure. KV/prefix caching stores repeated context to avoid re-encoding tokens; for reuse-heavy scenarios it reduces compute and latency. We'll show a simple example in the checklist.
04:50 Maya Ruiz: What about data retention? We need retention windows and the ability to opt out.
04:54 Sophie Chen: Hosted has a default retention policy but you can request shortened retention or disable for sensitive workloads. Private gives you full control. We'll include retention options in the security docs.
05:10 Lena Park: First-token timeline — can our devs realistically do it today?
05:14 Sophie Chen: Yes, steps: sign up, claim credits, run the Node sample; usually < 1 hour. If you want we can do a short pairing session.
05:24 Raj Patel: Any rate limits on sandbox keys?
05:27 Sophie Chen: Sandboxes have protective quotas but they’re generous; we can temporarily increase for benchmark runs.
05:36 Maya Ruiz: For SSO we use Okta and SCIM.
05:39 Sophie Chen: We support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for org accounts — we'll send setup steps.
05:50 Diego Morales: Quick question about model choice — are you looking at curated open models or private weights?
05:55 Lena Park: Prefer open models to avoid lock-in.
05:58 Diego Morales: We have verified open model variants; for quickstart we'll point you to a 13B quantized variant and a smaller 7B for latency tradeoffs.
06:20 Raj Patel: How do rollouts work if we want to test model versions?
06:24 Diego Morales: The Console supports traffic splitting, canary rollouts, and automatic fallback to a compatible variant if latency spikes or errors increase.
06:40 Maya Ruiz: For the pilot, what do you need from us?
06:43 Sophie Chen: Create an account, invite AE/SE, identify sample prompts and traffic pattern, provision test keys. Optionally whitelist Redwood IPs if you want controlled networking.
07:05 Lena Park: We'd like a 3-month pilot quote that includes a small Dedicated bucket.
07:10 Sophie Chen: We'll include a pilot pricing option; many teams start on Hosted and switch after patterns emerge.
07:20 Raj Patel: For Private/on-prem, what model formats and infra constraints exist?
07:24 Diego Morales: Private supports common formats and we help with conversion and quantization. On-prem may need specific kernel builds but we handle that during onboarding.
07:40 Maya Ruiz: KMS integration — we use AWS KMS; any HSM options?
07:44 Sophie Chen: Yes, we support AWS KMS and customer-managed keys in Private; HSM-backed keys available on enterprise tiers.
08:05 Diego Morales: Note on retrieval pipelines — if you plan RAG, test embeddings and reranking; Redwood offers embeddings endpoints and reranking support. We'll add example prompts.
08:30 Raj Patel: We'll include retrieval prompts in the bench.
08:45 (brief pause)
09:10 Sophie Chen: Circling back — Diego will share the bench checklist and harness, I'll send the quickstart link and free credits, and we'll schedule a POC kickoff next week.
12:00 Lena Park: Quick operational question — do you charge for embeddings differently?
12:07 Sophie Chen: Yes, embeddings have separate unit pricing; we'll include those numbers in the pricing sheet.
17:30 Raj Patel: We're worried about noisy neighbors on hosted; how isolated is Dedicated?
17:36 Diego Morales: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and isolation at the tenant level; predictable throughput and no noisy-neighbor interference.
22:00 Maya Ruiz: For the quickstart bench, can we use a smaller model and then switch to a quantized variant without changing prompts?
22:06 Diego Morales: Yes, typical flow is prototype on a smaller model then switch to a quantized variant; we keep API compatibility via model aliases so your code changes are minimal.
27:00 Lena Park: Any compliance paperwork we should expect for Private?
27:05 Sophie Chen: Private involves an onboarding questionnaire, network review, and security assessment — we'll send the checklist.
32:00 Raj Patel: On metrics, what do you surface in the Console during a bench?
32:05 Diego Morales: Token-level cost, latency p50/p95, per-route breakdown, and trace links. You can export logs for post-analysis.
37:00 Maya Ruiz: If we decide to commit to Dedicated, what's the billing cadence?
37:06 Sophie Chen: Monthly or annual commits supported. We'll include options in the pilot quote.
41:30 Sophie Chen: Final recap: Sophie sends Quickstart link + free credits + security pack; Diego shares benchmark checklist & sample prompts; Mariposa runs bench and shares results; we'll schedule POC kickoff (week of 2026-12-15).
41:50 Lena Park: Sounds good — thanks, everyone.
41:55 Sophie Chen: Thank you! We'll follow up by email with the links and next steps.
42:00 (call ends)
